c.tagline: Japan's cosmopolitan port city, where a futuristic bay skyline meets the country's largest Chinatown.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are strictly metered starting around ¥500; street hailing is common and reliable. Doors open automatically, and tipping is not expected.

emergency.note: Dial 110 for police and 119 for fire and ambulance/medical emergencies. English-speaking operators may be limited; the Japan Visitor Hotline (050-3816-2787) offers 24/7 multilingual support.

avoid.reason: In the Noge and Fukutomicho bar districts late at night, avoid touts and check bar prices before ordering; otherwise very safe.

hood_desc: Yokohama's gleaming waterfront district of skyscrapers, the Landmark Tower, Cosmo Clock 21 Ferris wheel, and Cup Noodles Museum; best for first-timers wanting modern sights, malls, and bay views all walkable.

The historic core around Kannai and Chinatown (Chukagai), home to Japan's largest Chinatown with hundreds of restaurants and temples plus the ballpark and old civic buildings; suits foodies and culture-seekers.

Elegant Motomachi shopping street below the leafy Yamate (Bluff) hillside of Western-style former foreign residences and the Harbour View Park; good for boutique shopping, cafes, and strolls with history.
The bustling commercial hub around Yokohama Station's west side, packed with department stores, restaurants, and nightlife; a convenient, well-connected base for transit across the city and to Tokyo.
The transit gateway around Shin-Yokohama Station with the Shinkansen stop, Nissan Stadium, and the Ramen Museum; a practical, quieter business-oriented area for onward bullet-train travel.
lodging: The Gate Hotel Yokohama by Hulic

water.note: Tap water is treated to strict national standards and safe to drink directly.

transit.hours: Trains and subways run from roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; there is no all-night service, so late-night travel relies on taxis.
transit.note: Yokohama is served by JR lines, private railways (Keikyu, Tokyu, Sotetsu), the Minatomirai Line, and the Yokohama Municipal Subway (Blue and Green lines), with the Sea Bass ferry linking waterfront stops.
transit.pay: A rechargeable Suica or PASMO IC card (also on smartphones) works across all trains, subways, and buses; single paper tickets and contactless credit cards are also accepted on many lines.

ferry: Sea Bass waterfront ferry (Yokohama Station - Minato Mirai - Yamashita Park)
train: JR lines, Keikyu, Tokyu, Sotetsu, Minatomirai Line, Yokohama Municipal Subway

transit.m: Airport Limousine Bus from Haneda (HND) to Yokohama City Air Terminal (YCAT) near Yokohama Station (~30 min)
Keikyu Airport Line train from Haneda to Yokohama Station (~25 min)
Narita Express (N'EX) or Airport Limousine Bus from Narita (NRT) to Yokohama (~90 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary anywhere in Japan and can cause confusion; excellent service is standard and included in the price.

food.name: Iekei ramen
food.desc: Yokohama's own ramen style, born here in 1974: rich pork-bone and soy broth, thick straight noodles, spinach, nori sheets and a slice of chashu.

places.name: Yoshimuraya
places.note: The 1974 originator of iekei; queues form early, so go off-peak.

places.name: Sugitaya
places.note: Long-running direct descendant shop, praised for a thicker, richer broth.

places.name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
places.note: Retro basement food hall where you can compare regional ramen styles.

food.name: Shumai
food.desc: Bite-size pork and scallop steamed dumplings, sold in boxed bento since the 1920s and treated as Yokohama's edible city symbol.

places.name: Kiyoken Honten
places.note: The 1908 institution behind the famous shumai bento; sit-down restaurant upstairs.

places.name: Kiyoken station kiosks
places.note: Grab-and-go boxes with the little ceramic soy-sauce gourd, a local ritual.

places.name: Manchinro Honten
places.note: Cantonese heritage house serving hand-made shumai and dim sum since 1892.

food.name: Chinatown dim sum and nikuman
food.desc: Japan's largest Chinatown turns out steamer baskets of dim sum plus fist-size steamed pork buns eaten standing on the street.

places.name: Heichinrou
places.note: Founded 1884, the oldest Cantonese restaurant in Japan; classic trolley dim sum.

places.name: Edosei
places.note: Street-corner nikuman shop with famously giant steamed buns; cash queue moves fast.

places.name: Chinatown main street
places.note: Roughly 200 eateries in a few blocks, best browsed hungry in the evening.

food.name: Sanmamen
food.desc: A Yokohama Chinatown invention: soy-based noodle soup crowned with a thick, glossy stir-fry of pork, bean sprouts and vegetables.

places.name: Gyokusentei
places.note: Widely credited as the birthplace of sanmamen; simple old-school dining room.

places.name: Chinatown noodle shops
places.note: Most Chinatown kitchens keep sanmamen on the menu year round.

food.name: Napolitan spaghetti
food.desc: Ketchup-glossed spaghetti with sausage, onion and peppers, invented in postwar Yokohama and now a nationwide comfort-food classic.

places.name: Hotel New Grand The Cafe
places.note: The hotel where napolitan was created; harbour-view room, still on the menu.

places.name: Center Grill
places.note: Yoshoku diner open since 1946, a local favourite for napolitan and hayashi rice.

food.name: Gyunabe beef hotpot
food.desc: Sweet-savoury beef simmered with miso and vegetables, the Meiji-era dish that first put beef on Japanese tables in this port city.

places.name: Janome-ya
places.note: Historic gyunabe specialist in the old Western quarter; reserve for dinner.

places.name: Ota Nawanoren
places.note: Trading since 1868, serving miso-based beef hotpot in tatami rooms.

food.name: Kirin beer
food.desc: Kirin has brewed beside Yokohama's waterfront since 1870, and the city now has a busy craft-beer scene to match.

places.name: Kirin Brewery Yokohama Factory
places.note: Free-to-book tour ending in a tasting of freshly poured Ichiban Shibori.

places.name: Yokohama Beer Umaya no Tavern
places.note: City brewpub pouring its own lagers and ales in a converted stable building.

places.name: Antenna America
places.note: Bottle shop and taproom with a deep US and Japanese craft list.

food.name: Chinese tea and bubble tea
food.desc: Chinatown teahouses pour oolong and pu-erh by the pot, while the same lanes are lined with tapioca milk-tea stands.

places.name: Yokohama Daisekai
places.note: Retro-styled complex with tea shops, sweets and a rooftop view.

places.name: Kanteibyo-dori tea shops
places.note: Cluster of tea merchants around the temple offering free tastings.

landmarks: Yokohama Landmark Tower
Once Japan's tallest building, this sleek 296-meter skyscraper offers a sky garden observatory with sweeping views over Minato Mirai and Tokyo Bay.
Cosmo Clock 21 (Ferris Wheel)
This giant illuminated Ferris wheel doubling as the world's largest clock is the glowing centerpiece of the Cosmo World amusement park and Minato Mirai's nighttime skyline.
Yokohama Bay Bridge
A striking cable-stayed suspension bridge whose illuminated white towers form one of the city's most photographed nighttime silhouettes over Tokyo Bay.
Yokohama Chinatown
The largest Chinatown in Japan, packed with ornate gates, lantern-lined streets, and vibrant temples that make for endlessly colorful photography.
Red Brick Warehouse (Akarenga Soko)
Beautifully restored early-20th-century brick warehouses turned into a lively shopping and event space right on the harbor.
Sankeien Garden
A sprawling traditional Japanese garden with relocated historic pagodas and teahouses set among ponds and seasonal blossoms.
Yokohama Marine Tower
A retro red-and-white lighthouse-style tower offering panoramic views and a nostalgic icon of the postwar port skyline.
Nippon Maru Memorial Park
A beautifully preserved four-masted sail training ship permanently docked as a floating museum beside the Landmark Tower.
Minato Mirai Skyline
The futuristic waterfront district's glittering cluster of towers and the Ferris wheel forms Yokohama's signature postcard view, especially at dusk.
Yamashita Park
Yokohama's oldest seaside park, a palm-lined promenade along the bay perfect for sunset strolls and harbor photography.

train.note: Japan is an island nation with no international trains. Long-distance trains use Shin-Yokohama, not the main Yokohama Station: all Hikari and Kodama and most Nozomi services on the Tokaido Shinkansen call there, and it is three stops from central Yokohama on the JR Yokohama Line or the Blue Line subway. From Tokyo, the JR Tokaido Main Line takes about 25 minutes for ¥470, the Tokyu Toyoko Line 26 minutes from Shibuya for ¥270, and the Keikyu Line is fastest at 18 minutes from Shinagawa for ¥300. Airport access is direct: the Narita Express runs through to Yokohama in about 1.5 hours for ¥4,290, and Keikyu's Airport Express reaches Yokohama Station from Haneda in 30-35 minutes for ¥480.

bus.note: There are no international buses from Japan. Highway and overnight coaches use YCAT, the Yokohama City Air Terminal beside the east exit of Yokohama Station, with services to Kyoto, Osaka, Nagoya, Sendai and the Kansai and Chubu airports, plus frequent limousine buses to Haneda and Narita. Book through Willer Express (https://willerexpress.com/en/) or the JR Bus group (https://kousokubus.net/JpnBus/en) in English; some Tokyo-departing overnight buses pick up at YCAT on their way south, which can save you a trip into Shinjuku.

ferry.note: Yokohama has no scheduled passenger ferry lines. Osanbashi Pier has customs, immigration and quarantine facilities, but it serves cruise ships rather than liner services, and the Daikoku and Shinko piers are cruise terminals too. The Sea Bass water bus between Yokohama Station East, Minato Mirai and Yamashita Park is an intra-city shuttle, not a way in or out. For actual voyages you go elsewhere in the bay: Tokyo's Takeshiba pier for the Izu and Ogasawara islands, or the Tokyo Bay Ferry from Kurihama near Yokosuka across to Kanaya in Chiba.

half.name: Kamakura
half.blurb: Former shogunate capital with the Great Buddha bronze statue and dozens of Zen temples in the surrounding hills.

half.name: Enoshima
half.blurb: Small tidal island reached by a causeway, with a shrine complex, sea caves, and coastal views.

half.name: Hakone
half.blurb: Hot spring resort town with volcanic sulfur vents, a crater lake, and views toward Mount Fuji.
